note: Pacing for the runner (scripts/pacing.py, D-486). The two budgets are PLACEHOLDERS: the plan's real limits are not published as token counts and Casey has not read them yet. They are in weighted tokens (see weights), sized from K9's measured tasks (a Sonnet worker plus an Opus review is about 0.5M to 1M weighted tokens). Replace them with measured figures once a usage limit has been hit and its reset recorded in state.usage.limit_hit, or once a quota command (PACING_QUOTA_CMD) reports utilisation, which then wins over this ledger. The runner sets PACING_QUOTA_CMD to quota_cmd_default when the variable is unset; scripts/quota_probe.py reads the session's own plan usage and is verified at the D-486 rehearsal (D-486). Calibration October 31, 2026 (D-1110): Casey read about 50% of the weekly plan used while this ledger stood at 102M weighted tokens (window from 2026-10-29T18:38Z, reset Thursday 2026-11-05T18:38Z), so the weekly budget is 200M until the quota probe (state.usage.source is still "ledger": the probe falls back silently) or a recorded limit_hit gives a better figure; the five-hour budget stays as it was for want of a reading. Spend line (D-1128, October 31): Casey wants the week's budget used up by Thursday morning, not run out early and then idle, so `spread` holds the week's spend to a straight line from the anchor reading (the ledger at 23:30Z, October 31) to the effective budget three hours before the reset; remove `spread` to return to claim-when-it-fits. Re-anchored November 1 (D-1167): the first in-band reading (D-1155) at 01:02Z said 59% of the week used, so the line now starts at 118M of the 200M week (plan units, the same unit the reading gives the pacer) and `headroom` drops from 0.1 to 0.03 so the line ends near 97% three hours before the reset the reading reports (2026-11-05T17:00Z), as Casey asked: no tokens left over on Thursday morning; the ledger, used only when no reading is under six hours old, sits about 12M below the anchor, so it does not restrain that one claim; the next session's reading pulls the line back. Hold removed November 1 (D-1189): Casey, 05:07 Phoenix, "from now on, you don't need to pause. If we run out early that's fine. Just don't work fast if slower produces a better result", so `spread` is gone and the pacer is back to claim-when-it-fits against the five-hour and weekly budgets (headroom 0.03 kept); the one lane, Opus workers and the single independent review are the slowness that buys accuracy, not idle time. Put `spread` back (anchor_at, anchor_used_week, finish_hours_before_reset) to hold a week to a line again. No five-hour budget November 11, 2026 (D-3056): Casey, about 19:15Z, "Also, I don't have a 5-hour token window, so don't worry about that" (earlier the same day: "Dont worry about the token budget. Just use the tokens efficiently"); the 30M five-hour figure was a placeholder that never had a reading behind it, and by 19:10Z it had about 3.8M left (ledger reset 20:04Z), room for about four tasks in flight, with the week at 72%. `budget_tokens_five_hour` is now null, which scripts/pacing.py reads as no five-hour window: it is left out of the estimate test, the standing and the projected finish (the ledger still counts it). A real reading (quota command or session reading) that reports the five-hour window at 100% still makes the pacer wait for its reset, and the week budget is unchanged. Set a number back to budget the five-hour window again.

actions_minutes.note: Nothing reads this block; it records the Actions limit for the next session (D-1451). The repository is public, and GitHub gives public repositories unlimited standard Linux Actions minutes, so Actions minutes do not limit the runner and nothing paces on them. Casey's decision on November 2, 2026, 01:02Z (docs/handoff/2026-11-02-evening.md): the repo stays public until the build is done, because a private repo would mean paying for minutes (about 25,000 a month at this pace against the plan's included figure). The keeper's sleeping job (D-1451) costs runner minutes but no money on a public repo. If the repository is ever made private, `private` holds the old figures (D-494: GitHub Pro, 3,000 Linux minutes a month included, about 35 minutes a cycle at Ci's ceiling); a keeper sleeping up to 5 h 40 m between cycles would then cost minutes too, so turn the keeper off or price it first.
